say.never: Merging brings another branch's commits into the branch you're on. You stand on the branch that **receives** them: be on `develop`, then merge `issue-7-auto-distance` into it.
say.bit: Merging brings another branch's commits into the branch you're on. Be on `develop`, then merge `issue-7-auto-distance`.

say.bit: After the merge, develop has the feature's commits too.

say.never: Click the **Source Control** icon on the left: the one that looks like a branch. It has one row per exercise folder.
Press **Ctrl+P**, type `03-merge/README` and press **Enter**. Opening a file from the folder makes its name show up in the bottom-left corner.
Look at the very bottom of the window. The name just left of the branch is the repository you're working on. Click it and choose **03-merge** from the list at the top.
say.bit: Bottom-left, click the repository name and choose **03-merge**.

say.never: The branch name beside it now belongs to that repository. It should say `develop`. If it says something else, click it and pick `develop`.
say.bit: The branch beside it should say `develop`. If not, click it and pick `develop`.

say.never: In Source Control, scroll the list until you can see the **03-merge** row.
On the **03-merge** row, click the **...** button (More Actions). Each row has its own, and it always works on that folder.
Point at **Branch** in the menu. A second menu opens beside it. Click **Merge...** there.
A list of branches drops down at the top. Click `issue-7-auto-distance`. Then open `Constants.java` in **03-merge**: `AUTO_DISTANCE_METERS` is there now.
Open Source Control and look at the **Graph**. It now shows the feature's commits sitting on `develop`. That's the merge, drawn as a picture.
say.bit: Open Source Control: the **Graph** shows the feature's commits now on develop.
